title: Back to the source
hook: picture nine: the river flows, the flowers are red (Ox-Herding 9)
tomorrow: stay on the quiet mountain, or walk into the market?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the empty circle: ox and herder gone, from the beginning not one thing. And then Kuoan keeps drawing.

Come home from a long trip and your own street looks strange for a day, then just right. Here's the puzzle in Kuoan's ninth picture. After the empty circle, you'd expect light, or nothing at all. Instead: a riverbank, a tree, flowers. And the verse scolds itself: too many steps taken to come back to the root and the source. Better to have been blind and deaf from the start. Why go back to plain things after the circle?
screen: `YOUR OWN STREET, STRANGE.` → `AFTER THE CIRCLE: A RIVERBANK.` → `TOO MANY STEPS.`

segments.voice: The answer is in the preface. From the beginning, it says, all was pure, without a speck of dust. The herder watches things grow and fade from a place of stillness. The waters are blue, the mountains green. He sits alone and watches them change. The verse ends: inside his hut he isn't looking for anything outside; the river flows on by itself, the flowers are red by themselves. Kuoan sounds almost sheepish: all that searching, catching, taming and riding, to arrive at what was there before the first step. That's the Zen teaching of return. Awakening doesn't trade this world for a better one; it hands this one back, as it is. A Chinese teacher, Qingyuan Weixin, put it in a saying recorded in Zen collections. Before he practiced, mountains were mountains and rivers were rivers. Then, with some insight, mountains were no longer mountains, and rivers no longer rivers. Now, at rest, mountains are just mountains again, and rivers again rivers. So the puzzle solves itself. The empty circle wasn't the end, because emptiness was never somewhere else. The river was flowing the whole time. Only the one looking changed.
screen: `PURE FROM THE BEGINNING.` · `THE RIVER FLOWS BY ITSELF.` · `MOUNTAINS ARE MOUNTAINS AGAIN.` · `ONLY THE ONE LOOKING CHANGED.` · then, large: `THE RIVER FLOWS.`

segments.voice: Look at some water, a glass of it will do, or a plant or a flower if one's near. For the two minutes, see it as just what it is, before any thought about it: water, wet; a leaf, green.
Back to the source: Kuoan's ninth picture. After emptiness, the world returns as it is: the river flows, the flowers are red.
The line to keep: the river flows, and it was flowing all along. Nine of ten.

howItsDone: Zen teachers point to plain things, mountains, rivers, flowers, as the place awakening is lived. People on this path look at ordinary things as they are.

chat.meaning: Kuoan's ninth picture returns to a river and red flowers after emptiness. Qingyuan: mountains are mountains again. Same world, seen as it is.
